issue: C1 sets a latency budget of ~500-800ms/turn achieved by 'stream LLM->TTS sentence-wise', and names TTS='edge-tts' without resolving WHICH concrete mechanism that means. Reading the actual code the design says to extend: apps/life-call/lib/voice-synth.cjs's `synthWakeClip()` invokes TTS by spawning a brand-new `python3 -m edge_tts` child process per call (execFile), writing an mp3 to a fresh mkdtemp dir, then shelling out to a SECOND child process (ffmpeg) to transcode -- each step has Python-interpreter-startup + disk-I/O + network-TTS-roundtrip overhead. If 'stream sentence-by-sentence' is implemented by literally repeating this subprocess-spawn pattern once per sentence (the only TTS mechanism that exists today to extend), 2-3 sentences/turn will very plausibly blow well past the stated 500-800ms/turn budget for TTS ALONE, before STT+LLM latency is even added. Separately, apps/life-call/package.json:13 already lists `msedge-tts` (a Node-native streaming Edge-TTS client) as an installed dependency, but it is UNUSED anywhere in apps/life-call (grep confirms zero requires/imports) and C1 never mentions it -- despite it being the obviously better-suited primitive for a genuinely low-latency streaming design. The spec asserts an aggressive, unsubstantiated latency number while pointing the implementer at the wrong (subprocess-per-call) TTS mechanism and ignoring an already-installed better one.
evidence: apps/life-call/lib/voice-synth.cjs:35-49 (execFile python3 -m edge_tts + execFile ffmpeg, per-call mkdtemp); apps/life-call/package.json:13 `"msedge-tts": "^2.0.6"` present but grep for msedge-tts usage across apps/life-call returns only package.json/package-lock.json (zero code references).
fix: Explicitly mandate the in-process streaming path (e.g. the already-installed `msedge-tts` Node client, or an equivalent that avoids per-sentence subprocess spawn + temp-file I/O) for the C1 turn loop, and either (a) justify the 500-800ms/turn number against that mechanism's measured latency, or (b) revise the budget to a number substantiated by an actual measurement noted in the evidence doc. Do not leave the implementer to infer this from the existing (deliberately different-purpose) one-way-clip synth path.
